transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because I just keep snapping at people, and it's getting to be a real problem. 

Like the other day, we had this safety meeting at work, and I just... I started yelling. It just came out before I could even stop myself. I'm an inspector on the floor, and now the younger inspectors act like they're scared to even come up and ask me a simple question. I don't want to be like that, but I just keep losing my temper.
Between your angry outbursts, do you return to your usual mood?

I'm not really sure. I mean... I guess I calm down eventually, but I don't know if I'd say I go back to my usual mood. I haven't really paid much attention to it, to be honest. I just sort of... get back to my line and keep working.
Have there been times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt rested?

No, I can't say that's ever happened. If I don't get enough sleep, I definitely feel it the next day. I've never had a time where I just didn't sleep much and actually felt rested... I'm usually pretty worn out if I don't get my rest.
Did these anger outbursts begin after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Yeah, they did. It's... well, this has all been going on since that machinery accident we had. It happened right after they made that overnight schedule change. So, it's been about two years and four months now.
How often do these angry outbursts happen?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of a specific number or anything like that. I just know it happens, but... I couldn't tell you if it's a certain amount of times a week or a month. I just haven't counted.
Do your angry outbursts happen mainly when something reminds you of the machinery accident or schedule change, or do they also happen in situations unrelated to those events?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed if there's a specific pattern to it. It... it might be when something reminds me of the accident, or it might just be other things that set me off. I just haven't really connected the dots to see exactly what triggers it every time.
Between the angry outbursts, do you feel persistently irritable or depressed most of the time?

I wouldn't say I feel like that most of the time, no. I mean, I have my moments, but... I don't think I'm just walking around feeling irritable or depressed all day, every day between those outbursts. It's more just when things boil over.
Is the machinery accident or any of its ongoing consequences still affecting your life now?

Yes, it definitely is. I mean... I’ve missed so many shifts at work lately. And I’ve lost so much patience with the trainees that I’m just no longer trusted to mentor the younger inspectors anymore. It's not just work, either. I’ve had to pull back from community theater, which I used to do a lot, just because... well, I can’t reliably get through the rehearsals.
Before the machinery accident, had you ever experienced similar angry outbursts?
No, not really. I mean, I'd get frustrated sometimes, like anyone else, but... nothing like this. These outbursts, they're new. I never used to lose my temper this way before the accident.
Are the effects of the machinery accident still an ongoing source of stress in your life today?

Well, yes, absolutely. Like I was just saying about my job and having to step away from the theater... it really is. It just feels like it's always hanging over me, so yeah, it's definitely a major stress in my life right now.
About how many separate angry outbursts have you had in the past 12 months?
I... I honestly couldn't give you a number. It's been a lot. Too many to count, really. It just happens so often now that I've lost track.
When you have an angry outburst, does it usually happen suddenly without a clear trigger, or does it typically follow a specific stressful event or provocation?

It usually happens suddenly. I just... I keep snapping at people. Like at a safety meeting we had recently, I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. There wasn't really a big provocation for it. And now the younger inspectors on the floor, they act scared to even come up and ask me anything. It just flares up before I can catch it.
Can you recall an angry outburst that happened when nothing related to the machinery accident, schedule change, or their ongoing consequences was happening?

No, I... I can't really think of one like that. Honestly, pretty much everything that sets me off seems to trace back to work, or the accident, or the whole mess with my schedule. I haven't noticed me blowing up over just... nothing, if it isn't tied to all that.
